_about: Seconds per character for each Olivia variant - the first row of the mode's timing table, which every later timing rule derives from (PHASE_PLAN.md section 3.2, step 2 criterion 2.6). Estimated from the fixtures' lengths; step 2 measures it. Nothing reads this file yet.
confirm: step 2 of the Olivia phase, criterion 2.6, from the demodulated fixtures
method: From assets/fixtures/olivia/manifest.json alone: each fixture's seconds, less 2.32 s where rsid is true, divided by the number of characters in its text, each newline counted as one. 2.32 s is the work instruction's figure for the RSID burst, and it agrees with data/rsid/rsid-codes.json: 15 tones plus 5 silent symbols either side, at a symbol rate of 10.7666015625 Hz, is 25 / 10.7666015625 = 2.322 s. Characters counted by machine: the CQ text is 38, the four-line QSO text 251.
why_an_upper_bound: A fixture's length includes whatever the transmitter sends before the first character and after the last - preamble, tail and the padding that completes the final block - so a length divided by a character count overstates the per-character time, and a short text overstates it most. The two 8/250 fixtures show it: the 38-character CQ gives 0.702 and the 251-character QSO 0.686. A straight line through both gives 0.683 s per character plus 0.72 s fixed; no other variant has two lengths to do the same.
